name: T7 bacteriophage
short_description: A smaller, simpler cousin of T4: the same icosahedral DNA-filled head, but a short, non-contractile tail stub with tiny fibres instead of an extendable injection apparatus. T7 is famous not for its shape but for one enzyme it carries: T7 RNA polymerase, one of the most widely used tools in molecular biology.

textbook.1: PASS on gemini-3-pro-image, first attempt. Regular ROUND icosahedral head (not prolate, correctly reads as round vs. T4's elongated head), DNA visible as dense golden coil in a quarter cutaway, small dark-navy internal-core cylinder visible at the head/tail junction, SHORT BLUNT tail stub (a stubby cone barely longer than wide, no ring striations, no contractile-sheath look, no hexagonal baseplate). FIBRE COUNT MEASURED: traced each leg from a grid-overlay crop of the raw PNG - six distinct kinked fibres confirmed, attached in a ring directly around the tail stub's rim (no baseplate hub), each shorter and closer to the body than T4's long sweeping legs. No lipid envelope, no starburst, no baked text, fills frame edge-to-edge on charcoal background, single specimen. Chosen as label base (svg_theme).

sem.1: PASS on gemini-3-pro-image, first attempt. Single specimen, false-colour surface-only SEM (correctly no internal cutaway, no DNA), round faceted icosahedral head, short blunt teal tail stub. FIBRE COUNT MEASURED: a tight zoomed crop (3x) of the tail-fibre cluster showed six separate kinked legs, each ending in a small cluster of globular beads matching the literature's description of the gp17 distal segment's four-globule array - counted explicitly: top, upper-right, lower-right, left, lower-left, bottom-centre = 6. No baked text/scale bar, fills frame edge-to-edge on dark substrate, no duplicate specimen.

reference: PASS - real negative-stain TEM of a single T7-like virion (ViralZone/SIB, photographer Hans-Wolfgang Ackermann, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0): a small, bright, angular (icosahedral) head silhouette with a faint short protrusion below it consistent with the short tail stub, against a dark stained background - genuinely a small, compact particle relative to the plate's own 100 nm scale bar, consistent with T7's ~55-60 nm head. The plate carries a baked-in 100 nm scale bar and a 'H.-W. ACKERMANN' text credit, so it is used unedited for provenance only and is NOT used as an SVG label base (per reference/svg-overlay.md, a micrograph with baked-in text should be cropped before use as a base - this one simply is not used as a base at all). Individual tail fibres are NOT resolvable in this micrograph at this resolution - the six-fibre count and ~30 nm fibre length used throughout the renders come from the structural literature (Steven et al. 1988 gp17 substructure paper, see render.md Sec 1), not from counting this photograph.

6 total render attempts on gemini-3-pro-image before acceptance - NOT the two unrecoverable failures (no starburst on any attempt; no border/frame on any attempt). MEASURED EDGE BLEED on the FINAL composed page (cairosvg render of t7-bacteriophage.coloring.svg at 800px, top 72% = the artwork area, outer 6px ink fraction, threshold 128): top 0.0000 -- not a defect, unreachable by construction, since the speech bubble sits in the page's top margin with white space above it on every coloring page in the atlas (confirmed project-wide across all 119 pages, see SKILL.md); bottom 0.042, left 0.138, right 0.078 -- genuine bleed on the three reachable edges, none forming a continuous full-length line. Two real, fixable defects were found and corrected across attempts: (1) attempts 1 and 4 filled the bacterium's open hatch solid black, violating the 'no solid fills except pupils' rule - fixed from attempt 2 onward by explicitly forbidding a filled hatch/porthole interior. (2) attempts 1-5 repeatedly rendered the six leg-stubs as either a continuous scalloped ruffle (attempt 1, uncountable), a tangled cluster with only 2-3 clearly separated feet (attempts 2-3), or a clean row of SEVEN separated legs instead of six (attempts 4-5, confirmed by grid-overlay counting each foot) - fixed on attempt 6 by explicitly specifying a 3-and-3 arrangement with a deliberate centre gap, which produced exactly six cleanly separated, individually countable straight capsule leg-stubs (grid-overlay count: feet at x=75,225,375 | gap | 675,825,975 on the raw PNG). Final accepted image: round-headed, low-sitting T7 character (small and stubby, clearly not lander-shaped like T4's) on 6 short blunt rounded leg-stubs, handing a small copied scroll through an already-open outline-only hatch to a smiling E. coli-planet character; no fight, no bursting, no violence.
